brief: GS's TMT desk notes a quiet Monday with US fixed income closed. HFs net sold US Info Tech at the fastest pace in 7 weeks, rotating out of Semis/Hardware and into Software and Industrials, while the long/short ratio and GS Sentiment indicator (-1.3 SD) point to lighter positioning even as the SPX sits within 1% of highs and the median stock is 16% below its own. A flight-to-quality bid (GS Quality factor +16% in 8 weeks, biggest since COVID) runs alongside that de-risking. TMT's internal debate: compute demand outstripping supply still supports 2027+ capex conviction, but execution questions are growing, including around the Personal Agent theme. Separately, GS research argues high-performance NAND (HBF) could ease the AI inference memory wall, sizing a $40-150bn TAM by 2030 and large hyperscaler capex savings from a ~30% lower inference cost. GS also likes its Power Up America power basket on low positioning and normalized valuation. The note additionally reports, without taking a stance, an AMZN-Decart AI acquisition in talks, Nadella's AI 'emergency brake' remarks, CXMT's memory progress, Google's internal Gemini 4 build, Houthi strikes near Riyadh, a disputed Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, record EWZ Brazil volume, and this week's earnings/CPI calendar.
